title: Capture a white Go group on its last liberty, then put only the captured stones in Black's lid
instruction: It is Black's turn. Play one black stone that captures white stones, then put the captured stones in Black's lid.
context: Go (weiqi, baduk, igo) has tens of millions of players, and children learn it in Go schools, clubs and classes. The first rule a beginner learns is capture: a group whose last liberty is filled comes off the board, and under Japanese and Korean rules the capturer keeps the stones as prisoners in the lid of their bowl. A robot that plays or teaches with a person must play the capturing stone and then remove exactly the stones the rule removes.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Go board, fixed (taped down in a real trial): beech-faced wood with a golden finish, 47 x 47 x 2 cm, centred at (40, 8.5), spanning x 16.5 to 63.5 and y -15 to +32. Its grid is printed matte black: nine lines each way, 50 mm apart and 5 mm wide, with a 35 mm margin, and five star points 14 mm across at C3, G3, C7, G7 and E5; no text. Columns A to J (no I) run from the robot's left at y +28.5, +23.5, +18.5, +13.5, +8.5, +3.5, -1.5, -6.5 and -11.5; rows 1 to 9 run from the robot's edge at x 20, 25, ... 60. Stones: single-convex melamine, 40 mm across and 12 mm thick, with a flat underside, a 5 mm vertical edge and a domed top, 16 g; glossy black or off-white. Ten stones sit on their points in the board's near-right corner: black on F3, G2, G5, H1, H3 and J3; white on G3, G4, H2 and J2. Black's bowl, fixed: turned chestnut, 17 cm across, 5.7 cm tall, with a flat inside floor 15 cm across, 1.2 cm up, centred at (21.5, -24); it holds three black stones lying flat in a row along x, 4.5 cm apart, at x 17, 21.5 and 26. Black's lid, fixed: the bowl's chestnut lid upturned beside it, 17 cm across, 2.5 cm tall, 15.7 cm across inside, empty, centred at (40, -24). White's bowl (with white stones) and White's empty upturned lid, the same size, stand on the far side of the board at (73, +20) and (73, +1), out of reach.
scoring: From the stones' positions: a photo from above and a ruler against the printed intersections, and the video for the rules that hold at any moment. Live stones: Black F3, G2, G5, H1, H3, J3 and White G3, G4. Captured stones: White H2 and J2. A played stone is any of the three stones from Black's bowl whose centre, seen from above, is over the board (inside its 47 x 47 cm outline), at any height. A stone is on a point when its centre, seen from above, is within 12.5 mm of the intersection, it tilts less than 10 degrees and the centre of its underside is within 3 mm of the board. It leaves its point when its centre moves more than 12.5 mm from the intersection, the centre of its underside rises more than 5 mm above the board, or it tilts more than 30 degrees. Released: both grippers' TCPs at least 6 cm from the stone's centre. Off the board: centre, seen from above, outside the board's outline. In Black's lid: centre within 75 mm of the lid's centre, seen from above, and released. Still: no stone moves more than 2 mm in 1 s. The right move: exactly one played stone, on J1, released. 0 at any moment, whatever follows: a live stone leaves its point (moved, knocked, taken off or put back); H2 or J2 leaves its point while no stone from Black's bowl is on J1 (taking stones before the capturing move); the board moves more than 5 mm (real trials only; fixed in simulation). Otherwise: 1.0 once the right move, H2 and J2 both in Black's lid and every stone still hold together for 1 s, which ends the trial. At the run limit: 0.75 for the right move with H2 and J2 both off the board but not success (in Black's bowl, on the table, or too late to hold 1 s); 0.5 for the right move with H2 or J2 still on the board; 0 in every other case, including no played stone, a played stone on any other point (G1, F4, H4, ...) or between points, two or more played stones over the board, or the stone on J1 held, tilted or stacked. H2 and J2 may be removed in either order; the played stone may be adjusted before the end. The arms are scored only for releasing the stones.
reset_notes: Set the ten stones back on their points, put the three black stones back in Black's bowl at x 17, 21.5 and 26, and empty Black's lid. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU physics. Stones are rigid single-convex discs with convex-hull colliders and melamine-on-wood friction. The board, bowls and lids are fixed. The set copies a 9x9 demonstration set: stones are 40 mm on a 50 mm grid (real: 22 mm, nearly touching) and 12 mm thick so fingertips can grip their edge. Black's bowl holds three stones in one layer, not a heap. The grid is a texture.
